goal_status: Active; no official score or SOTA claim established.
question: Does nonuniform discrete physical profiling explain cosmology-dependent false alarms, and can normal-only score correction help?
scope: Authorized erdos-3242 lab only; all four hosts used for the frozen field closure study. RAM-backed folders; no GCS or production changes.

literature.application: Best-fit physical-model goodness-of-fit is a useful inference control. We compare discrete and continuous per-map fits, keeping every neural weight fixed; our energy score is not an exact chi-squared test or likelihood ratio.
Retain the existing independent field-level model as a complementary detector; its simplified research setting does not establish our competition performance.
Architecture and local image correlations can make generative likelihood unreliable for OOD; better normal fit does not guarantee better anomaly detection.
Scattering is effective in real weak-lensing parameter inference, but our prior R2 scattering ablation did not clearly improve OOD probes. This round does not duplicate that completed experiment.

fixed_models: Three R3 four-noise-view 30000-update summary flows; unchanged two field networks and regional specialist.

physical_profile.inputs: Two standardized physical conditioning coordinates per individual map, no true labels at deployment.
physical_profile.algorithm: Four best original-grid starts, 128 projected Adam steps, convex hull of the 101 training cosmologies, best iterate retained.
physical_profile.numerics: 202 normal pilot maps: exact singleton/order/chunk agreement; independent projection check; dense 1964-point reference on 16 maps; 64-vs-128 iteration check.
physical_profile.finding: Continuous profiling changes scores only slightly. False-alarm variation persists when using known true cosmology as a normal-only diagnostic; grid discretization is not its main explanation.

normal_score_correction.fit: 3232 normal validation maps; no calibration or audit maps fit the regression.
normal_score_correction.input: Mean inferred standardized cosmology from the three frozen networks; target is log mean profile energy.
normal_score_correction.selection: Five folds grouped by cosmology. Checkpoint selection had already used these validation maps; the scale CV is conditional on cross-fitted location residuals, not fully nested whole-pipeline CV.
normal_score_correction.finding: Location correction explains a small part of normal log-score variance. Additional variance-model NLL improvement is small. Two-sided typicality reduced sensitivity in these tests and was not promoted.

fresh_noise_closure.reproducibility: All four independently prepared observation caches had identical hashes. Every observation was scored once by each of the two field models, checked by shard coverage and file hashes.
fresh_noise_closure.finding: Corrected hybrid improves seven of eight point estimates, with a real IAAFT regression. The spatial variant improves spatial modulation from 0.5410 to 0.5903 but also loses IAAFT sensitivity. Neither dominates every shift.

candidates.08: Continuous-profile, normal-score-corrected summary + unchanged field residual; equal normal-scaled average.
candidates.09: Maximum of normal-scaled 08 and the unchanged regional specialist.
candidates.prior_candidates: 04/05/06/07 unchanged; each expresses different inductive assumptions.

implementation_audit.resolved_issue: A duplicate compare.py module name caused an import failure in the initial R4 wrapper. Fixed R3 runtime import precedence; closure then passed. No model or score settings changed.

limitations: Synthetic diagnostics and clean audit maps are reused; fresh measurement noise is not a fresh cosmological simulation.
Bootstrap intervals are conditional empirical IID intervals, excluding model-selection uncertainty and unseen physical alternatives.
Normal correction does not make false alarms uniform across every cosmology.
Continuous inferred physical coordinates can absorb anomaly signals. Scores are heuristic, not exact conditional p-values.
IAAFT preserves valid-pixel histograms but not masked Fourier amplitudes exactly.
Private-evaluation interface and clean installation remain unverified.
next_questions: Test sparse coordinate violations or local geometry of the normal latent representation; aggregate energy may hide changes in a small number of informative directions. Keep noise and nuisance effects controlled.
Test whether a better field representation improves morphology sensitivity without removing the useful normal score correction.
Characterize score corrections on independently simulated normal/alternative physics if such permissible data become available.
Validate actual competition performance of frozen candidates; no official performance has been observed.
turn_audit: Progress: completed profiling experiment, normal-only correction, independent numerical checks, and frozen four-host fresh-noise/precision comparison.

packaged_predictions.public_test_use: Independent frozen inference and numerical verification only; no fitting, normalization, ranking or selection.
packaged_predictions.timing_limit: Reuses prior field inference; timing is not the full cost of fresh inference on 10000 maps.
